newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: South Korean gov't raises local LNG, LPG prices.
newsitem.headline: South Korean gov't raises local LNG, LPG prices.

text.p: South Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy said on Monday it will raise domestic prices of liquefied national gas (LNG) and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) starting Tuesday.

Retail prices of LNG will rise by 9.7 percent to 269.47 won on average per cubic metre from the current 245.73 won, and those of LPG by 17.6 percent to 600 won per kilogram from 510 won, a ministry statement said.
Wholesale prices of LNG will gain 15.3 percent.
The ministry blamed rising import prices of LNG and LPG and the Korean won's fall against the dollar for the price rises.
The prices were last raised in August 1995.
